resolvedFinding.fact: The first new cgroup hook directly read self.cgroup_parent. EngineImageSmoke manually initializes without ImageSmoke.__init__ and calls ImageSmoke.start_container from its own create_environment, so that source raised AttributeError.
resolvedFinding.correction: Inherited hook reads use getattr(..., None); no optional pin means the original Engine command has no cgroup argument. PostgreSQL optional selection uses the same compatible default.
resolvedFinding.regressionSource: InheritedContainerOptionsTests exercises the real Engine constructor/create_environment and explicit base-constructor PostgreSQL/cgroup options with a fake Docker transport. Reviewer did not execute these tests.

reviewedSecretBehavior: The sole runtime call receives a password generated with secrets.token_urlsafe(32) by the owned Engine fixture. CLI inputs select images/revision/context/output, not a deployment credential.

Native Linux/amd64 and an actual writable host tmpfs are admitted before the sole runtime write. Descriptor-held nofollow ancestors, private0700 owner directory, exclusive single-link0600 leaf, literal plaintext write, flush,0444 and identity rechecks remain unchanged.

Failure cleanup keeps descriptor ownership and removes only the original inode; ordinary completion removes the private temporary directory after owned fixture cleanup. Abrupt failure and trusted same-UID/root actors retain the documented residuals.

The new hook changes neither generated password sources, environment filtering, diagnostic redaction, cleanup ownership nor the visible plaintext sink/caller closure. Explicit pinned PostgreSQL switches only the selected native image and pull policy; explicit cgroup selects one constrained flat fixture slice.

The workflow still has contents:read, persist-credentials:false, no deployment environment/production credential input, no registry push, a native fixture deadline, and retained failure artifacts. No source query annotation or alert dismissal is introduced.
residuals: Generated passwords remain plaintext during the real _FILE fixture, including existing Docker arguments/environments. Runner UID, host root and Docker daemon are trusted; tmpfs may swap and abrupt failure may bypass cleanup.
A later Docker bind resolves a pathname. Same-UID/root name substitution after verification and non-atomic cleanup against that actor are not eliminated.

This finite source review does not execute the Engine, prove native lifecycle behavior, establish current CodeQL finding disposition, qualify installed custody, or authorize deployment. Exact-source tests/native checks/managed scanner and named-ref findings remain required.
